summary: Sao Htun Hmat Win was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw. He taught at the University of Yangon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs (attested 2002).

Sara L. McClintock specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD 2002 under Tom J. F. Tillemans), she has held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2003) and Emory University.
Sara Marie Conrad is a scholar in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her MA at Indiana University, where Elliot Sperling served on her committee.
Sarah Aoife Richardson is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2016 under the supervision of Jenny Purtle.

Sarah E. Fraser specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, and she held appointments at Northwestern University (1996) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2000).

Sarah Harding is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (~1976–1989) and Drubpön Lama Tenpa (~1976–1980), and she held a post at Naropa University from circa 1992 to 2008.

Sarah J. Horton specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied under Stanley Weinstein at Yale University and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

Sarah Jacoby is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University (~1993–1997) and the University of Virginia (~2000–2007), holding posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (2009).

Sarah Shaw is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. In 2013, she was affiliated with Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.
Saraju Rath is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1914–1980) was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He held posts as librarian at the Asiatic Society and as a faculty member at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied civil engineering at Presidency University, Kolkata (~1869–1874), and received instruction from Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Palden Chöpel.
Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Manipur University (attested 2006) under the supervision of S. Shyamkishore Singh.
Saroja Bhate (b. 1942) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University from circa 1989 to 2002 and was attested there again in 2011.
Sarva Daman Singh is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who held posts at the University of Queensland, serving as professor of history in 1958 and attested there in 1987.

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was an Indian philosopher and Indologist educated at Madras Christian College. He held posts at Presidency College, Mysore, Calcutta, Oxford (1936–1939), BHU (vice chancellor, 1939–1948), Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (~1944–1975), and the University of Delhi (chancellor, 1953–1962).

Saswati Mutsuddy is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served as an assistant professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).

Satiranjan Sen, a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied at Peking University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti. He held a post as a research scholar and junior research fellow at Visva-Bharati University.

Satischandra Vidyabhusana (1870–1920) was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a PhD at the University of Calcutta under Sarat Chandra Das. He served as principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at Presidency University, Calcutta University, and the Asiatic Society.

Satoru Harada (b. 1947) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA from the University of Tokyo (~1970–1974). He held posts at the Toyo Bunko (1978), Eastern Institute (1982), and Kokushikan University (~2001–2017).
